papers.title_in_file: Direct Generation and Detection of Correlated Photons with 3.2 um Wavelength Spacing
papers.version_note: arXiv v2 (13 Sep 2017). The file title drops 'Quantum' relative to the record file name; the content is the expected paper.
sections_read: 3 Coincidence measurement of quantum correlated photon pair
Methods: Experimental setup for photon-pair generation
Methods: Noise photon counts for different time-frequency modes

figures.shows: (a) Cross-section schematic of the SiO2-clad LiNbO3 ridge waveguide with labelled dimensions D, TLN, WB, WT, WC, TSiO2. (b) Line plot of upconverted power (a.u., 0 to 1) against pump frequency offset (about -0.2 to 0.2 THz): experimental points and a dotted fitted/simulated curve, a single central peak at 0 THz with full width of roughly 0.1 THz and small side lobes. (c) Three simulated mode-intensity maps (651 nm, 780 nm, 3950 nm) over about -2 to 2 um (horizontal) and -7 to 7 um (vertical), each a single compact fundamental lobe centered in the core.
figures.confirmed_by: The measured phase matching results are plotted in Fig. 1 (b), where a clear phase-matching peak is shown.

figures.shows: Experimental setup: a 651.2 nm, 130 ps, 10 MHz pump pulse laser feeds the SPDC PPLN; an RF synchronization links it to a 779.8 nm, 130 ps, 10 MHz upconversion pump. Output at 779.8 nm goes through a 780 nm filter set to a Si-APD; the 3950 nm idler goes through a 3950 nm bandpass filter, is combined at a dichroic mirror with the upconversion pump, and enters the upconversion PPLN. The upconverted light passes a 650 nm filter set to a second Si-APD. Both Si-APDs feed a time-to-digital converter.
figures.confirmed_by: Figure 2 shows a schematic of the experimental setup

figures.shows: (a) Photon-pair probability per pulse (y, about 0.002 to 0.012) against SPDC pump peak power (x, about 2 to 13.5 mW): seven black data points on a linear fit line rising from about 0.002 at about 2 mW to about 0.012 at about 13.5 mW. (b) Bar histogram of signal-photon arrival time (x, 0 to about 1500 ps) against photon counts (y, x10^3, 0 to 25): one peak of about 21 thousand counts near about 350 ps, with a low tail of about 1 thousand counts at later times.
figures.confirmed_by: Figure 3 (a) plots the measured signal-photon generation probability as a function of pump peak power, which displays a linear dependence, as expected.

figures.shows: (a) Internal conversion efficiency (y, 0 to about 0.35) against upconversion pump peak power (x, 0 to about 4.5 W): red triangles (experiment) rise from about 0.03 at about 0.4 W to a maximum of about 0.34 at about 3.9 W, then fall to about 0.30 at about 4.4 W; the blue simulation line rises from 0 to about 0.32 at about 4 W and lies above the data at low and mid power (about 0.15 against about 0.10 near about 2 W). (b) Noise photon probability per pulse (y, 0 to about 0.009) against upconversion pump peak power (x, about 0.4 to 4.4 W): blue points increase monotonically from about 0.0001 to about 0.0084.
figures.confirmed_by: The result as a function of the upconversion pump peak power is shown in Fig. 4(a)

figures.shows: (a) Coincidence histogram, counts (y, 0 to 30) against time (x, 0 to about 2700 ps), red with idler input and blue without: red shows a peak of about 27 counts near about 1350 ps over a background of about 2 to 4 counts per bin; blue stays near the background. (b) Coincidence counts (y, 0 to about 400) against SPDC pump peak power (x, about 2 to 13.5 mW) for measured (red), accidental (green) and true (blue) coincidences: the true and measured ones rise roughly linearly from about 20 at about 2 mW to about 280 at about 13.5 mW (about 190 at about 9.7 mW); the accidental ones stay below about 20 with a quadratic fit in the inset. (c) CAR (y, about 10 to 70) against pump peak power: about 16 at about 2 mW, about 22 at about 4 mW, about 40 at about 6 mW, about 53 at about 7.7 mW, about 54 at about 9.7 mW, about 33 at about 11.5 mW, about 17 at about 13.5 mW, with error bars.
figures.confirmed_by: Figure 5(a) plots a typical coincidence histogram between two Si-APDs

figures.shows: (a) Noise photon histograms, counts (y, 0 to 9000) against time (x, 0 to about 2200 ps), over 100 s: green peak about 7800, red peak about 6500, blue peak about 450, all near about 1100 ps. (b) Photon counts (y, x10^4, 0 to 18) against upconversion pump peak power (x, about 5.4 to 10 W), with linear fits: green rises from about 5 to about 17, red from about 4 to about 12.7, blue from about 0.3 to about 1.6. The caption labels green as 144 modes, red as 724 and blue as 2900 modes.

papers.what_it_is: An experimental paper reporting room-temperature SPDC in a PPLN waveguide giving 779.8 nm and 3950 nm photon pairs, with the 3950 nm photons detected by a PPLN upconversion detector and a Si-APD, and a coincidence-to-accidental ratio of 54.

assertions.value: The authors report direct generation and measurement of correlated photons spaced by as much as 3.2 um in wavelength, between 780 nm and 3950 nm, using only room temperature devices.
quotes: Here we report on direct generation and measurement of correlated photons spaced by as much as 3.2 um in wavelength, between 780 nm and 3950 nm, using only room temperature devices.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study experimental demonstration.

assertions.value: The authors state that the SPDC process downconverts a 651.2 nm pump photon to a 779.8 nm signal photon and a 3950 nm idler photon.
quotes: For the current SPDC process where a 651.2 nm pump photon downconverts to a pair of a 779.8 nm signal photon and a 3950 nm idler photon.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own experimental configuration.

assertions.value: The authors state that the pair detuning is over 3.2 microns, or >300 THz, which they describe as the largest detuning thus far in any waveguide-based photon source.
quotes: The detuning of the pair is over 3.2 microns, or >300 THz, which is the largest detuning thus far in any waveguide-based photon source.
assertions.certainty_reason: Priority claim by the authors, with no survey of other sources in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that the waveguides have a silicon-dioxide cladded core with 3.5 um height (D) and 11 um top width (Wt) ridge structure, so that all lightwaves are in their fundamental quasi-TM modes for maximum overlap.
quotes: a silicon-dioxide cladded core with 3.5 um height (D) and 11 um top width (Wt) ridge structure
so that all lightwaves are in their respective fundamental quasi-transverse-magnetic (quasi-TM) modes for the maximum overlap
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own device geometry.

assertions.value: The authors state that the waveguide is periodically poled with a domain length of 16.7 micron to achieve quasi-phase matching for the fundamental transverse modes, offsetting the group-velocity-induced phase mismatch between signal and idler.
quotes: the waveguide is periodically poled with a domain length of 16.7 micron to achieve quasi-phase matching
there is a large group velocity difference between the signal and idler photons
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own device design.

assertions.value: The authors state that the SPDC waveguide temperature is stabilized at 32.2 ± 0.1 degrees C for optimum phase matching, and the upconversion waveguide at 62.2 ± 0.1 degrees C.
quotes: stabilized at 32.2 ± 0.1
with temperature stabilized at 62.2 ± 0.1
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own operating conditions.

assertions.value: The authors state that the SPDC pump is a 651.2 nm pulse train with 10 MHz repetition rate and 130 ps pulse width, coupled into a 2.2-cm long PPLN waveguide.
quotes: A 651.2 nm pulse train with 10 MHz repetition rate and 130 ps pulse width is coupled
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own pump parameters.
assertions.reader_inference: The caption gives a 2.2-cm waveguide length, but the Methods mention a 25-cm long MgO:PPLN waveguide for pump generation; these look like different devices, but the paper does not say so.

assertions.value: The authors state that the 3950 nm photons are measured by an upconversion detector in which another PPLN waveguide converts them to 651 nm, detected by a second Si-APD, with a 779.8 nm pump.
quotes: Instead, our 3950 nm photons are measured by an upconversion photon detector, consisting of another PPLN waveguide to convert them to 651 nm for detection in a second Si-APD.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own detection scheme.

assertions.value: The authors state that the upconversion pump is a 779.8 nm pulse train with 130 ps pulse width and 10 MHz repetition rate, synchronized with the SPDC pump.
quotes: a 779.8 nm pulse train with 130 ps pulse width and 10 MHz repetition rate that is synchronized with the SPDC pump
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors give two values for the 3950 nm idler bandpass filter bandwidth: 90 nm in the Figure 2 caption and 60 nm FWHM in the Methods.
quotes: (bandwidth: 90 nm; extinction: 70 dB)
FWHM bandwidth: 60 nm
assertions.certainty_reason: The two stated values disagree and the paper does not reconcile them.
assertions.reader_inference: An internal inconsistency in the stated idler filter bandwidth.

assertions.value: The authors report that, from the slope of the signal-photon generation probability against pump peak power, the SPDC efficiency is estimated to be -87 dB.
quotes: is estimated to be -87 dB, meaning that about one in every 5 × 108 pump photons
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study measured efficiency.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract-level -87 dB corresponds to about 2e-9 pairs per pump photon, consistent with the roughly 0.01 pair probability per pulse seen in Figure 3(a) at about 13.5 mW peak power and 130 ps pulses.

assertions.value: The authors report that the measured signal-photon generation probability depends linearly on SPDC pump peak power, as expected.
quotes: Figure 3 (a) plots the measured signal-photon generation probability as a function of pump peak power, which displays a linear dependence, as expected.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study measurement.

assertions.value: Read from Figure 3(a): the photon-pair probability per pulse rises roughly linearly from about 0.002 at about 2 mW to about 0.012 at about 13.5 mW of SPDC pump peak power, following a linear fit.
quotes: Measured signal photon generation probability as a function of the SPDC pump peak
where black dots are the experimental data and the black solid line is a linear ﬁt.
assertions.certainty_reason: Values read by eye from a plot.

assertions.value: The authors report a signal single-photon pulse of 130 ps FWHM after the filters, with an effective spectral bandwidth of 3 nm (FWHM), corresponding to effectively 100 detected time-frequency modes.
quotes: shown a single-photon pulse of 130 ps full width at half maximum (FWHM) after the
provide an effective spectral bandwidth of 3 nm (FWHM), so that there are effectively 100 detected time-frequency modes
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study measurement.
assertions.reader_inference: Later sections use 144 detected modes for the idler path, so the number of detected modes differs between the signal and idler descriptions.

assertions.value: Read from Figure 3(b): the signal-photon arrival-time histogram shows a single main peak of about 21 thousand counts near about 350 ps, with a low tail of about 1 thousand counts per bin out to about 1500 ps, integrated over 100 s.
quotes: Histogram of the signal photon arrival time by the means of time-correlated single photon counting
assertions.certainty_reason: Values read by eye from a plot.

assertions.value: The authors state that there is no available photon detector for the mid-IR photons at room temperature, and that existing mid-IR detectors require cryogenic cooling.
quotes: there is no available photon detector for the mid-IR photons at room temperature
assertions.certainty_reason: Background statement attributed to prior work, not tested here.

assertions.value: The authors report that the phase matching bandwidth of the upconversion waveguide is measured to be 5.6 nm (FWHM), corresponding to 107 GHz.
quotes: The phase matching bandwidth of the waveguide is measured to be 5.6 nm (FWHM), corresponding to 107 GHz in spectral bandwidth.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study measurement.
assertions.reader_inference: Figure 1(b) shows a central lobe of roughly 0.1 THz width, consistent with this value.

assertions.value: The authors report an internal upconversion efficiency of 33.9 ± 1.8%, the highest value, at an upconversion pump peak power of 3.8 W.
quotes: 33.9 ± 1.8% achieved at the peak pump power of 3.8 W
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study measurement, derived from signal counts and independently measured losses.
assertions.reader_inference: The efficiency is inferred (not measured directly) from the correlated signal-photon rate, the characterized losses and Si-APD quantum efficiencies, so it inherits those uncertainties.

assertions.value: The authors report that the conversion efficiency decreases as the upconversion pump power further increases beyond the maximum, and attribute this saturation likely to multiple spatial modes for the photons.
quotes: decreases as the power further increases
is likely due to the existence of multiple spatial modes for the photons
assertions.certainty_reason: Measured trend with a hedged explanation that is not tested.

assertions.value: Read from Figure 4(a): the experimental internal conversion efficiency rises from about 0.03 at about 0.4 W to about 0.34 at about 3.9 W and falls to about 0.30 at about 4.4 W; the no-free-parameter simulation rises to about 0.32 at about 4 W and lies above the data at low to mid power, for example about 0.15 against about 0.10 near about 2 W.
quotes: It shows a good agreement with experimental results
achieved at the peak pump power of 3.8 W
assertions.certainty_reason: Values read by eye from a plot.
assertions.reader_inference: The text calls the discrepancy slight; the plot shows a simulation overestimate of up to about 0.05 in efficiency at mid power.

assertions.value: The authors report that a modal decomposition of the joint spectral function gives a total number of SPDC modes of about 15, approximately equal to BT/4, with B the SPDC waveguide phase matching bandwidth and T the SPDC pump pulse temporal width.
quotes: to be about 15, approximately equal to BT/4, with B the phase matching bandwidth of the SPDC waveguide and T the temporal width of the SPDC pump pulses
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result from the authors' own model.

assertions.value: The authors report that their simulation of the upconversion, with no free fitting parameter, agrees well with the measured efficiency, with the slight discrepancy likely due to higher-order spatial modes of the pump and waveguide propagation loss, both neglected in the simulation.
quotes: It shows a good agreement with experimental results, with the slight discrepancy likely due to the existence of higher-order spatial modes for the pump pulses
both of which have been neglected in the present simulation
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' comparison of their own simulation with data.

assertions.value: The authors report that, at 33.9% conversion efficiency, the noise photons are approximately 6.5×10−3 (ten to the minus three) per pump pulse for the 144 detected modes entering the Si-APD.
quotes: the noise photons are approximately 6.5×10−3 per pump pulse for the 144 detected modes entering the Si-APD
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study measurement.
assertions.reader_inference: The Methods give about 3.8×10−4 per pulse for 144 detection modes at optimum conversion efficiency, and the abstract-level introduction gives 2.6×10−6 per time-frequency mode. These do not match 6.5×10−3 divided by 144, about 4.5×10−5, so the noise figures are mutually inconsistent or defined differently.

assertions.value: The authors state that the noise can be lowered substantially to 4.5x10−5 (ten to the minus five) per pulse if the number of detected modes is reduced to 1, by shorter pump and SPDC pulses or narrower bandpass filters for the upconverted photons.
quotes: This can be lowered substantially to 4.5x10−5 per pulse if the number of the detected modes is reduced to 1
assertions.certainty_reason: Projection, not measured with a single detected mode.
assertions.reader_inference: The value equals 6.5×10−3 divided by 144, so it is a rescaling, not a measurement.

assertions.value: The authors report in the Methods a noise detection probability of about 3.8×10−4 (ten to the minus four) per pulse with 144 detection modes at optimum conversion efficiency, including detector dark count, upconversion noise and blackbody radiation.
quotes: The noise detection at optimum conversion efﬁciency is about 3.8×10−4 per pulse with 144 detection modes
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study measurement that disagrees with the main-text figure.
assertions.reader_inference: This is about 17 times lower than the 6.5×10−3 per pulse in Section 2 for the same 144 modes and efficiency, and Figure 4(b) at about 3.8 W reads about 0.0065, matching the main text.

assertions.value: Read from Figure 4(b): the noise photon probability per pulse rises monotonically with upconversion pump peak power from about 0.0001 at about 0.4 W to about 0.0065 at about 3.8 W and about 0.0084 at about 4.4 W.
quotes: Figure 4(b) shows the number of noise photons created by the upconversion pump.
assertions.certainty_reason: Values read by eye from a plot.

assertions.value: The authors report a total detection efficiency of the 3950 nm single photons of approximately 0.078% for the current under-optimized setup.
quotes: the 3950 nm single photons is approximately 0.078% for the current under-optimized setup
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study estimate from losses and efficiencies.

assertions.value: The authors state that the idler detection efficiency can be improved to 2.5% by using parabolic mirrors with a shorter focal length to reduce total waveguide coupling loss by 6 dB and Si-APDs with over 80% quantum efficiency.
quotes: to 2.5% by replacing the present parabolic mirrors by ones with a shorter focal length
Si-APD’s with over 80% quantum efﬁciency
assertions.certainty_reason: Projection not tested in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors report that the total loss from the output of the SPDC waveguide to the output of the upconversion waveguide, measured with weak coherent 3950 nm light, is about 16 dB.
quotes: The total loss from the output of the SPDC waveguide to the output of the upconversion waveguide is measured to be about 16 dB
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study measurement.

assertions.value: The authors state that they determine true upconverted idler-photon counts by subtracting counts with SPDC off from counts with SPDC on, to separate them from Raman-scattered photons.
quotes: we record the total single photon counts with the SPDC on and off, from which the true-upconverted idler-photon counts are derived through subtraction of the latter from the former
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own measurement procedure.

assertions.value: The authors state that Raman scattering photons of the pump falling in the signal band are not expected to be significant, owing to the pump-signal detuning of more than 2500 per cm.
quotes: large detuning between the pump and signal wavelength of more than 2500
assertions.certainty_reason: Expectation citing prior work, not measured here.

assertions.value: The authors report that the noise count was measured without idler input at approximately 144, 725 and 2900 detected time-frequency modes, and that the noise count is linearly dependent on the upconversion pump peak power.
quotes: We measure the noise photons without the input of the idler photons with approximately 144, 725 and 2900 detected time-frequency modes
is linearly dependent on the pump peak power
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study measurement.
assertions.reader_inference: The text says 725 modes while the Figure 6 caption says 724.

assertions.value: The authors state that the majority of the dark counts come from spontaneous Raman scattering of the upconversion pump pulses falling in the bandpass filter window, since the Si-APD intrinsic dark count and afterpulsing probability are negligible.
quotes: the majority of the dark counts are from the spontaneous Raman scattering of the upconversion pump pulses that falls in the window of the bandpass
assertions.certainty_reason: Attribution stated without a separate measurement of the Raman contribution.

assertions.value: Read from Figure 6(b): noise photon counts over 100 s rise linearly with upconversion pump peak power from about 5.4 to 10 W; at about 10 W the green series is about 17 x10^4, the red series about 12.7 x10^4 and the blue series about 1.6 x10^4. The caption assigns green to 144, red to 724 and blue to 2900 modes.
quotes: Histograms of the noise photon detection for 144 (green), 724 (red) and 2900 (blue)
the noise count rate is higher with wider bandpass
assertions.certainty_reason: Values read by eye from a plot.
assertions.reader_inference: With the caption's labels the 144-mode series has the highest counts and the 2900-mode series the lowest, which is the opposite of the text claim that wider filters give higher noise; the labelling or the text appears to be in error.

assertions.value: The authors define a coincident detection as both Si-APDs clicking within the coincidence window and an accidental coincidence as both clicking outside the window; true coincidences are total minus accidental coincidences.
quotes: A coincident detection is registered when both Si-APD’s click within the coincidence window.
when both Si-APDs click outside the coincidence window
are obtained by subtracting the accidental coincidence from the total coincidence
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own definitions of coincidence quantities.

assertions.value: The authors report that true coincidence counts depend linearly on the SPDC pump peak power, while accidental coincidences depend quadratically on it.
quotes: the true coincidence is linearly dependent on the pump power, as expected for SPDC
and thus depends quadratically on the pump peak power
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study measurement.

assertions.value: The authors report a maximum coincidence-to-accidental ratio (CAR) of 54±7 at a peak power of 9.7 mW, limited by uncorrelated noise photons and dark counts of the upconversion detection system.
quotes: A maximum CAR of 54±7 is obtained at a peak power of 9.7 mW, limited by the uncorrelated noise photons and dark counts of the upconversion detection system.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study measurement.

assertions.value: The authors report that at lower pump power the CAR is only around 10∼20, attributed to the low pair generation rate relative to the total dark count rate, and that at high pump power multiphoton generation raises accidental coincidences and lowers the CAR.
quotes: the CAR is only around 10∼20, which attributes to the low photon-pair generation rate relative to the total dark count rate
the multiphoton effect involving the simultaneous generation of more than a photon pair increases the probability of accidental-coincidence detection
assertions.certainty_reason: Measured trend with authors' unverified explanation.
assertions.reader_inference: Figure 5(c) reads about 16 at the lowest power, so 'around 10 to 20' fits the plot; the dark-count and multiphoton explanations are not separately tested.

assertions.value: Read from Figure 5(c): CAR rises from about 16 at about 2 mW pump peak power to a maximum of about 54 at about 9.7 mW, then falls to about 33 at about 11.5 mW and about 17 at about 13.5 mW; error bars are about 5 to 10 in CAR.
quotes: coincidence-to-accidental coincidence ratio versus pump peak power
A maximum CAR of 54±7 is obtained at a peak power of 9.7 mW
assertions.certainty_reason: Values read by eye from a plot.

assertions.value: The authors state that the CAR can be improved by reducing the number of detected time-frequency modes of the signal and idler photons to 1.
quotes: It can be improved by reducing the number of detected time-frequency modes of the signal and idler photons to 143.
assertions.certainty_reason: Projection not tested; the printed '143' appears to be 'to 1' followed by reference 43.

assertions.value: The authors report a true coincidence count of 275 within an integration time of 300 s at the highest CAR of 54 ±7.
quotes: At the highest CAR of 54 ±7, we obtained a true coincidence count of 275 within an integration time of 300 s.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study measurement.
assertions.reader_inference: Figure 5(b) reads about 190 to 200 true coincidences at about 9.7 mW and about 280 only near about 13.5 mW, so 275 does not match the plotted true counts at the CAR maximum.

assertions.value: The authors report a photon pair production rate of about 9.4 × 104 pair per second (exponent printed flat), using total detection efficiencies of 1.3% for the signal and 0.078% for the idler.
quotes: the photon pair production rate is about 9.4 × 104 pair per second
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study derived rate.
assertions.reader_inference: 275 counts in 300 s divided by 1.3% × 0.078% gives about 9×104 per second, consistent with the quoted rate, but it depends on the 275 count that Figure 5(b) does not clearly support.

assertions.value: The authors report a spectral brightness of 4.4 × 102 pair/s/nm/mW (exponent printed flat).
quotes: with spectral brightness of 4.4 × 102 pair/s/nm/mW
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study derived figure.
assertions.reader_inference: Dividing 9.4×104 pairs per second by the 3 nm filter bandwidth and 9.7 mW gives about 3×103, not 4.4×102; the paper does not show how the brightness is defined.

assertions.value: The authors state they expect to improve the production rate and spectral brightness by two orders of magnitude by using GHz-repetition-rate pump pulses.
quotes: We expect to improve the production rate and spectral brightness by two orders of magnitude by simply using GHz-repetition-rate pump pulses.
assertions.certainty_reason: Projection not tested.

assertions.value: The authors state that a CAR of 54 gives a Franson visibility of 96% in the context of time-energy entanglement, on par with existing SPDC sources in visible and near-IR.
quotes: This gives a Franson visibility of 96% in the context of time-energy entanglement35, which is on par with existing SPDC sources in visible and near-IR.
assertions.certainty_reason: Derived from CAR by formula; no Franson interferometer measurement is reported.
assertions.reader_inference: The 96% value is computed as (CAR-1)/(CAR+1) from the measured CAR; no two-photon interference or entanglement measurement is reported, so entanglement is not demonstrated.

assertions.value: The authors state that the correlation measurement yields a coincidence to accidental ratio of 54, which they say indicates high quantum-state purity of the pairs.
quotes: yields a coincidence to accidental ratio of 54, which indicates high quantum-state purity of the pairs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Interpretation of CAR as purity, not tested separately.
assertions.reader_inference: CAR indicates pair-to-noise ratio, not state purity in the density-matrix sense; no state tomography is reported.

assertions.value: The authors state that by detecting the 780 nm photons, mid-IR photons can be generated via heralding with g2(0) = 0.08, making a high-quality single photon source in mid-IR.
quotes: mid-IR photons can be generated via heralding with g2(0) = 0.08
assertions.certainty_reason: Inferred value; no heralded g2 measurement is shown in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper cites a reference for the g2 value and shows no heralded correlation measurement, so the g2(0) of 0.08 ± 0.015 is inferred from the measured CAR.

assertions.value: The authors state that substituting a PPLN crystal for the waveguide could translate the photon-pair correlation to the spatial domain for heralded or quantum ghost imaging in mid-IR.
quotes: a PPLN crystal, the same strong correlation of the photon pairs can be translated to the spatial
assertions.certainty_reason: Proposed application, not tested.

assertions.value: The authors state that, combined with appropriate quantum error correction or privacy amplification, the SPDC scheme can be readily applicable for free-space QKD based on time-energy entanglement in the mid-infrared spectrum.
quotes: our SPDC scheme can be readily applicable for free-space QKD based
assertions.certainty_reason: Prospective application not tested in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: No QKD run, free-space link or entanglement test is reported; the claim rests on the CAR-derived visibility.

assertions.value: The authors cite prior work that light around 4 micron experiences much less scattering and scintillation than other commonly used wavelengths in free-space links.
quotes: light around 4 micron has been measured to experience much less scattering and scintillation
assertions.certainty_reason: Result attributed to another work.

assertions.value: The authors state that only very recently photon pairs have been generated at 3.1 microns, with similar wavelengths and rather limited correlation.
quotes: Only very recently, photon pairs have been generated at 3.1 microns
assertions.certainty_reason: Result attributed to another work.

assertions.value: The authors state that broadband, mode-shaped pumping pulses can let the upconversion detector selectively upconvert signal photons over interfering noise overlapping in time and spectrum; this is not demonstrated in the present experiment.
quotes: Furthermore, by using broadband, modeshaped pumping pulses, it can also selectively upconvert the signal photons over interfering noises
assertions.certainty_reason: Attributed to the authors' earlier work (reference 34); not tested here.

assertions.value: The authors state that adopting the quantum optical arbitrary waveform technique for pair generation and upconversion detection will potentially improve the CAR by >20 times (to over 1000).
quotes: which will potentially improve the coincidence-to-accidental coincidence ratio by >20 times (to over 1000)
assertions.certainty_reason: Future-work projection, not tested.

assertions.value: The authors report that the Si-APD has 50 ps timing resolution, while the time-to-digital converter has 66 ps root-mean-square timing resolution and 27 ps time-bin resolution.
quotes: The Si-APD has 50 ps timing resolution while the TDC has 66 ps root-mean-square timing resolution and 27 ps time-bin resolution.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own instrument parameters.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that they have demonstrated direct generation and detection of high-purity photon pairs across the visible/near-IR (780 nm) and mid-IR (3950 nm) spectra, using only room-temperature optics.
quotes: We have demonstrated direct generation and detection of high-purity photon pairs across the visible/near-IR (780 nm) and mid-IR (3950 nm) spectra, using only room-temperature optics.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' summary of their single-study result.
assertions.reader_inference: 'High-purity' rests on CAR 54, which is a pair-to-noise measure, not a state-purity measurement.

assertions.value: Read from Figure 1(b): the measured upconversion phase-matching profile is a single peak at zero pump-frequency offset with a full width of roughly 0.1 THz, with experimental points following the fitted curve and small side lobes near about ±0.13 THz.
quotes: The measured phase matching results are plotted in Fig. 1 (b), where a clear phase-matching peak is shown.
assertions.certainty_reason: Values read by eye from a plot.
